page: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the server bundles a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM, alongside 1880 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference for small and medium models, particularly in prompt processing and text generation for 135M and 7B parameter models. It registers strong multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench, alongside strong database operations and Redis SET throughput. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed during large-scale workloads; while prompt processing for a 70B model remains strong, text generation for the same 70B model falls into the bottom 25% due to the single-GPU configuration and 22 GB VRAM limitation. Memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks and single-threaded decompression tasks remain in the average tier.

The hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of multi-GPU configurations. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, a single L4 GPU, and local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance appropriate for medium-scale machine learning inference, ray tracing, image processing, software compilation, and database operations.
